title: I got Disrespected
transcript: Knight takes D3 is an incredible mistake by Black that loses the game on the spot. But before I can explain to you why, we need to understand what this game is. You see, I was just minding my own business on YouTube when I saw this live stream of Elena and Tushar playing chess online, and Tushar decided to personally attack me like this. >> Let's go. Petro is there. I actually think she can beat you. >> I simply could not accept this disrespect, so I accepted the challenge. But here is the trick, they sent me a position where I was going to play without both of my knights. But I am not the kind of person to turn down challenges. So we started playing. I controlled the center, developed the pieces, and I tried to go for a four-move checkmate, which Elena spots. Now, I castle and I keep bringing my pieces out, and I am just trying to create some chances for my pieces to create some attacks. Here I play bishop to H6. You cannot take the bishop because it's pinned, and I am threatening a checkmate in one move. But Elena finds knight to H5 attacking the queen and defending the checkmate threat at the same time. So I play queen to F3 counter-attacking the knight so that if now you take the bishop, I'm going to take. But instead, Elena just went back with her knight, and now I recreated my threat, which means that if she doesn't want to repeat moves and draw the game, she has to play G6. Now, if you ever find yourself in a situation where you have to play a games with odds, don't trade pieces. Even if you're winning material, this bishop is so much more valuable than this rook. So I didn't even take the rook and instead developed my other rook, and so did Elena. I prepared to double my rooks, but unfortunately, after bishop to D6, now my queen is under attack and the rook is under attack, which forces my hand, and now I have to take the rook. If queen takes, I am going to take the bishop, so the knight dropped back. Now I move my queen, and after the knight jumps back, I developed the other rook. And now you might notice that there is quite a lot of activity with these white pieces, but unfortunately, Black is of course still completely winning being up an overwhelming amount of material, but fools will resign. And so, after knight to f4, attacking the queen, and queen to f4, I saw my opportunity after knight takes d3. You see, at first glance, this move seems to make a lot of sense, because you are opening a discovered attack on the queen, while also forking the rook and the queen. But, Elena and Tooshar, master forgotten who they were dealing with, because in this position, I played the majestic, incredible, sublime, and beautiful queen takes f6, sacrificing my queen completely, while also leaving my rook to hang. And yet, believe it or not, black is completely lost. >> Oh! >> If you take the rook, this is just going to be a checkmate in one move. And finally, if the queen is captured, there is going to be a checkmate in two. After rook to e8 check, bishop to f8, rook f8 is a beautiful checkmate. And this was the only game we played. Don't even bother go check the game history.
